description: An agent-native red-teaming workspace with a fast browser, direct HTTP traffic control, sandboxed execution, and auditable sessions. Pure Rust.

written.description: Gives an agent a browser that controls its own network traffic, so the model can capture, edit, replay and compare the requests a web app sends without a proxy in between. Each session runs under a network policy and records every fetch it allowed or refused.

alive.last_commit_message:
support proxy with agent-browser (#679)

* implement proxy

* support the Chromium capture proxy on macOS

Linux still prints an agent-browser command that trusts only the session CA.
macOS prints --ignore-https-errors, because agent-browser cannot install that
CA there. Document the proxy lane and drop the removed login-mode references.

* fix the capture-proxy clippy failure and date the changed docs

observe_proxy_response took eight arguments, so both clippy jobs failed.
The response is now one ProxyResponse. The host-selection test no longer
asserts a cfg! constant. features/ and manual/ record 2026-09-29.

* name ring when the browser builds its TLS client

A workspace build enables both ring and aws-lc-rs on rustls, and rustls then
refuses to pick a process default. The TLS tests panicked before the handshake.
The browser client now builds its config with ring directly.
